articles.headline: DDG Apologizes On Behalf Of Kanye-Recreating Fan Who Crashed Streamer Awards
keyFacts: A fan crashed the Streamer Awards stage during AriAtHome's acceptance speech to claim nominee DDG deserved the award instead.
DDG publicly apologized on social media for the interruption, and AriAtHome responded by accepting the apology.
Other streamers criticized the event's security following the incident, while the venue has faced prior safety concerns.
body: On Thursday night, the sixth annual Streamer Awards were held in Los Angeles, honoring the most popular online personalities, Twitch streamers in particular. A gala filled with reaction and drama farmers will inevitably attract its own share of troublemakers, but this year one stage crasher decided to pull out an old classic. Recreating Kanye Westâs infamous MTV stunt, a man took to the stage during AriAtHomeâs acceptance speech, saying that nominee DDG was more deserving. Shortly after, DDG squashed any potential, second hand beef by apologizing on the fanâs behalf.
i do not co-sign or approve of what happened during ur award bro. ur very talented and clearly deserved it. My apologies ð¯ð @ARIatTWIT
— DDG (@PontiacMadeDDG) November 13, 2026
“I do not co-sign or approve of what happened during ur award bro,” posted DDG, “ur [AriAtHome] very talented and clearly deserved it. My apologies.”

Darryl Dwayne Granberry, better known as DDG, was nominated for this yearâs Best Music Streamer award, alongside PlaqueBoyMax and Bishu. The award went to Ari Miller, better known as AriAtHome. Partway through Millerâs acceptance speech, an unknown individual took to the stage, grabbing the microphone. “Iâm sorry imma let you finish but DDG had the best music of all time,” the crasher said.
Man who interrupted ARIatHOME on stage at the Streamer Awards to say DDG should've won the award, releases his POV through recording sunglasses ð³
While exiting he gets into an argument with Marlon. pic.twitter.com/NCPcdG0LmD
— yoxic (@yoxics) November 13, 2026

A clear nod to Kanye Westâs infamous MTV Music Video Awards snafu from 2009, where West cut off Taylor Swift to say BeyoncÃ© was robbed, the individual donned smart glasses, a $700 long sleeve and live streamed the incident from his goggles. While Miller appears to be a good sport, nodding and letting him hang out to dry, the fan received jeers from the crowd. On his way out, the individual got into a verbal altercation with streamer Marlon Lundgren Garcia, who called him “corny as fuck.” After Granberry posted his apology, Miller responded in kind, writing “nothing but love bro.”

In the days following, other streamers have criticized the awards for allowing someone to easily raid the stage. The Streamer Awards are held in tandem with TwitchCon. While unaffiliated beyond convenient timing, both events seem to suffer similar security woes. The convention itself seems to be hurting from low ticket sales after years of safety issues, whether itâs stalker concerns or hazardous ball pits.

The winner of this yearâs Streamer Award was the immensely popular IShowSpeed, who wasnât in attendance due to a missed flight. If anyone deserved a stage crasher on their behalf, it was the GoOffKings, who deserve more flowers for “DVD week.”

articles.headline: Is away goals rule used in Concacaf Nations League? Tiebreaker explained
keyFacts: The away goals rule remains in effect for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, unlike in UEFA competitions.
Four semifinal spots are at stake as teams compete in two-legged matches to determine the winners.
If aggregate scores and away goals are tied after 180 minutes, extra time and penalty shootouts will decide the outcome.
body: The away goals tiebreaker may not be used in Europe anymore, but it's still up and running in Concacaf.
The Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals take place over the next several days, with four semifinal spots on the line.
The quarterfinals will be staged over two legs, with each team hosting a match. If the aggregate score is tied after 180 minutes of play, the team with more away goals will advance.
Away goals scored during extra time do not serve as an additional tiebreaker, so if the teams remain level after extra time, the series goes to penalties.

Per Concacaf regulations, "if the aggregate score is tied after both legs, the away goals rule will apply. If the tie remains level, extra time will be played, followed by a penalty shootout, if necessary, to determine the winner."
That is in contrast to UEFA, which has removed the away goals tiebreaker for its club and international competitions.

articles.headline: Niclas Fullkrug lined up for permanent West Ham exit after outscoring Harry Kane
keyFacts: Werder Bremen boss Daniel Thioune stated the club intends to keep forward Niclas Fullkrug beyond next summer.
Fullkrug has scored nine goals in nine appearances this season during his loan spell from West Ham United.
His recent goalscoring form earned him a recall to the Germany national team under manager Jurgen Klopp.
body: Werder Bremen boss Daniel Thioune has signalled his intention to keep Niclas Fullkrug beyond next summer.
The German forward is currently in his third spell at the Bundesliga side having joined on loan from Championship club West Ham United .
Fullkrug has rediscovered his form in his third spell with Bremen Getty
Fullkrug has run riot so far this season , already netting nine goals in nine appearances to help Bremen sit sixth in the table.

He currently leads the Golden Boot race ahead of Bayer Leverkusen forward Patrick Schick who has eight goals, whilst Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is in joint-12th with just four league goals thus far in the 2026/27 campaign.
And Thioune has now publicly stated that the club would like to re-sign Fullkrug on a permanent basis.
“I believe the desire is shared by all sides,” Thioune. “We as a club, I as coach, and Niclas himself are all very interested in continuing to work together beyond the summer.”

Fullkrug ‘s return to goalscoring form is a welcome one after netting just three times in 29 appearances in all competitions for the Hammers since signing from Borussia Dortmund for £27million in 2024.

His time in East London was tough as a result of injuries and inconsistent playing time, with him even launching an explosive rant in the direction of his own teammates when the Irons drew with an already-relegated Southampton back in April 2025.

A mid-season loan to Serie A giants AC Milan in January of this year was not the fresh slate he had hoped it would be, with him scoring just once in 20 appearances as his parent club were relegated from the Premier League in his absence.
Fullkrug recalled to Germany national team
Fullkrug ‘s recent goal-scoring prowess earned him a recall to the Germany national team for the first time since September 2025, and his first selection by new manager Jurgen Klopp .

“Good form and scoring goals are never a bad thing,” Klopp answered when asked why he had brought Fullkrug back. “Fulle has been performing and scoring all kinds of goals, almost all of them spectacular. “

Klopp added: “He has an incredible influence on the game, not just through his goals, but also the way he carries himself, I don’t think he was able to have that influence on a team at every stage of his career, at Bremen, he can.
Bremen are keen to make Fullkrug’s loan move permanent next summer Getty
“When you feel at home, you can see what happens. That’s generally the feeling we want to give the players, even if we don’t have them together very often.”
Fullkrug ‘s most successful spell of his career came playing for the River Islanders, in which he scored 45 goals in 90 appearances between 2019-2023.
Of Bundesliga players with at least 20 shots this season, only Eintracht Frankfurt forward Younes Ebnoutalib has a higher xG per shot than Fullkrug (0.26 to 0.21).
“I was delighted because he thoroughly deserves it,” Thioune said of his feelings when he found out Fullkrug was called up for international duty this November.

“If you look at his individual performances, he’s been one of the standout attacking players. He’s earned this call-up through his own hard work. I’m proud to have a Germany international in our squad.”
For Fullkrug , there is perhaps just one simple explanation as to why he has rediscovered his knack for goal – feeling at home.
Fullkrug has just three goals in 29 appearances for West Ham since signing in August 2024 Getty
“ Werder is simply my home, ” he told reporters during the DFB press conference on Tuesday. “It’s my footballing home. As you all know, one sleeps the best in one’s own bed.
“I immediately felt comfortable there. I joined the academy at the age of 14 and, in my estimation, I believe about 70-90 percent of the same people are on staff there.”
He also ensured that he gave the Bremen medical staff their flowers for keeping him fit and healthy since his arrival.
“I’m healthy and there’s a medical department there that takes good care of me,” Fullkrug continued. “They’ve managed to get me back on track and ensure that I haven’t missed any training sessions.
“And we have a great team from which I benefit. The transfers that we brought in this summer have all done great. I just happen to be one of them.”

articles.headline: Magic Is Bringing Back Its Most Controversial Creature Type
keyFacts: Vice President of Design Aaron Forsythe revealed during MagicCon: Atlanta 2026 that more Sliver creature cards are returning to Magic: The Gathering.
Forsythe stated that developers have a plan for the cards, though he did not share a specific timeline for their release.
Slivers are a controversial creature type that can quickly scale in power, making them difficult to develop and balance.
body: Whether you love or hate Sliver decks in Magic: The Gathering, you should prepare for more Sliver cards to make their way to the game soon. Vice President of Design Aaron Forsythe revealed as much during an in-person interview with Polygon at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026.
More Sliver cards are coming to Magic: The Gathering

During an interview at MagicCon, Polygon mentioned how a couple of Sliver-related cards that were part of Edge of Eternities, and asked if the Magic: The Gathering team is thinking about bringing the cards back in a big way or if they are too broken to actively support. In response, Forsythe confirmed that "we know when they’re coming back," although he wouldn't share a specific timeline for their return.

"They will be back," Forsythe elaborated. "We know when they're coming back, and I'm not going to tell you. But we know people love them. They are hard to develop. They are hard to make work unlimited, but we have a plan."

Slivers have a long history in Magic: The Gathering as one of the most fun yet controversial creature types that a player can use in their decks. Sliver cards actively boost or benefit from other Sliver cards, enabling decks that can quickly scale up in power in a way that's tough to counter or beat.

As Forsythe mentions, that makes them particularly tough to develop, since they can be very overpowered. That is likely why we haven't seen as many Sliver cards in recent years. Wizards of the Coast now seems up to the challenge of bringing Sliver cards back in a big way, though, and it'll be fascinating to see what form the comeback that Forsythe teased takes.

While we have no idea when more Sliver cards will come to Magic: The Gathering, Wizards of the Coast did debut the Nauctis: The Sunken Realm set of cards at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026. That set will be released on Feb. 5, 2027, and will introduce a whole new oceanic realm to the game's multiverse.
Additional reporting by Corey Plante and Jake Kleinman

articles.headline: Got an iPhone Duo? These 9 settings make it easier to use
keyFacts: TechCrunch reports that Apple's new iPhone Duo foldable device lacks Face ID and requires users to rely on Touch ID for authentication.
TechCrunch recommends adjusting settings such as registering extra fingerprints and enabling Apple Watch unlock to make Touch ID easier to use.
TechCrunch notes that users can also improve everyday tasks on the iPhone Duo by adjusting volume controls, back tap for screenshots, and camera settings.
body: Apple’s new foldable, the iPhone Duo, has proven popular enough that the company can’t keep the device in stock. While the Duo introduces a new way to use an iPhone, getting the most out of this initial version may require adjusting a few settings to make it work better when it comes to everyday tasks, like unlocking the device with Touch ID, navigating the interface, and taking photos.
After spending some time with the Duo, we’d recommend making the following adjustments to make the new iPhone a bit easier to use, most notably when it comes to the use of Touch ID.
Settings to make it easier to live with Touch ID

Unlike modern iPhones, the Duo doesn’t support Face ID. That means you have to adjust to pressing a finger on the side of the device once again to authenticate with apps, unlock the device, and use Apple Pay. But there are a few things you can do to make the switch back to the older technology a bit less painful.

- Register extra fingerprints: This may seem like an obvious suggestion, but if you’re used to just registering a fingerprint or two with Touch ID, prepare to rethink that strategy with the Duo. Because the device can be held in multiple orientations, flipped both horizontally and vertically, and because of the small size of the Duo’s screen, you may find that a lot of your fingers (and thumbs!) can now reach the Touch ID button. We’d recommend holding the device in your hand and turning it in different ways, then register the fingerprints where you end up holding the device the most — on both hands. Yes, setting up Touch ID can be a bit tedious compared with Face ID, as there are multiple prints to register. Still, it’s a one-time setup, and later on you’ll be glad that you took the time to make more of your fingerprints work. To register a fingerprint, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Add a Fingerprint.

- Unlock with Apple Watch: If you’re in the market for the iPhone Duo, there’s a good likelihood that you own other Apple devices, like the Apple Watch. If that’s the case, you’re in luck because you can use your Watch to unlock the Duo without having to bother with Touch ID. This will save you time and frustration in the long run, so get used to wearing your Apple Watch more often, especially when you’re out and about and don’t want to fiddle as much with finger placement. To use the Apple Watch unlock, your watch will need to be passcode-protected and worn near your phone. To turn this feature on, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Unlock with Apple Watch.

- Rest finger to Open: This is an optional setting, not necessarily a “must” like the above, but we’ve found it useful. The “rest finger” setting is actually an accessibility feature, but it can double as a usability feature, too. When enabled, you only have to rest your finger lightly on the Touch ID sensor to unlock the device, instead of having to press down. Those who prefer this setting find it can make unlocking the phone faster and more convenient, but others may disagree, as they like the more tactile sensation of a button press. Try it both ways and see which one fits you best. To enable this one, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Rest Finger to Open.
Usability Improvements

There are a few settings that could also improve your experience with the iPhone Duo, as they may make it easier to perform certain everyday tasks, like taking screenshots or reaching different parts of the screen, among other things.

- Turn off Fixed Volume Controls: This is a favorite hack for new Duo owners, as it makes using the device in any orientation much easier. By default, the iPhone Duo’s volume buttons are “fixed,” which means that no matter how you rotate the device, the Volume Up button remains the button that increases the volume and the Volume Down button decreases it. But many people find it’s easier if the buttons’ functionality rotates with the device. That is, the buttons re-orient themselves based on how you are holding the phone, making the “up” option always on the top or right. As you fold, unfold, and flip the phone, having buttons that flip with you actually makes more sense. To turn off the fixed volume controls, go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Fixed Position Volume Controls.

- Back Tap for Screenshots: The Duo tries to make it easier to take a screenshot by pressing the side button and either the Volume Up or Volume Down button at the same time. However, you still might find the process a two-handed affair (unless you just ask Siri to do it for you). That’s why many Duo owners are turning to a buried Accessibility feature to make taking screenshots a bit less complicated. In the phone’s accessibility settings, you can configure whether a double tap or triple tap on the back of the device triggers a particular action — which you can set to ‘take a screenshot.’ (Some people prefer the triple tap so they don’t accidentally trigger the feature.) Once enabled, you could hold your Duo in one hand, then use a finger to tap on the back of the phone to take the screenshot, saving you a bit of the hassle that comes with managing the button combinations. To configure this, go to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Back Tap > then choose a double or triple tap and your action. (Screenshot is under the “Device” menu.)

- Reachability: This is another accessibility feature that some Duo owners like to configure, but others like to have off. The option was originally designed to make larger-screened devices easier to use with one hand, which makes it sometimes hard to reach, depending on your hand size. Typically, when Reachability is turned on, the iPhone will lower the top half of the screen to make it easier to reach with your thumb. The Duo does things a little differently, though. Because the phone is wide — it’s shaped like a passport — it’s the far side of the screen that’s harder to reach than the top. So when you turn on Reachability, you will instead be able to swipe the left or right edge of the screen to bring a side into reach. We should note that this feature is enabled by default, but if you find yourself accidentally triggering it and want to turn it off, you can under Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

- Lock when folded: This one is more of a personal preference, we’ll admit. But if you tend to unfold the device when you’re working with it, then snap it closed when you’re done, you might like to configure a setting that will automatically lock the screen for you when the device is folded shut. However, doing so requires you to create a new shortcut, as there isn’t a setting for this — at least, not yet.

- To make the shortcut, you’ll open the Shortcuts app, tap the plus (+) sign, then the Edit button in the upper-right. You then tap into the search bar, and tap on the word “automation” that appears in blue under the search bar that appears at the top of the screen. Next, you’ll scroll down until you find the option “Opened or Closed” under the Display section. Tap that, tap on the word “Opened” to change it to “Closed,” then tap in the search bar at the bottom again and type in “Lock Screen.” Tap on the option

“Lock Screen” when it appears in the search results, and you’re done — the shortcut has been made. You can tap on the play button here to test it, if you’d like. And if you ever change your mind, just delete the shortcut!
Special Camera Tricks
The camera tricks are a little more niche, but some Duo owners have found the following to be helpful.

- Customize Camera Controls: The iPhone Duo lets you customize the on-screen layout of the camera controls in the Camera app itself, as part of the latest iOS software update. To use this feature, you’ll open the Camera app and open the six-dot Camera Controls menu in the bottom right. You then tap on the plus sign at the top of the menu (or to the right or left depending on how you’re holding the phone!). This lets you pick and choose which of the camera tools appear above the camera frame itself for quick access, like the flash, or the option to enable or disable Live Photos, or whether Night Mode is on or off, among other things. You can then drag those options to create whichever order makes the most sense for you. (Note: this feature is not exclusive to the Duo.)

- Disable Smart Take Flash: The Smart Take feature on the iPhone Duo is designed to help you take hands-free group or solo shots without having to use a self-timer. Instead, you prop up the Duo on a stable surface and activate Smart Take by pressing the button. The camera will detect when there’s movement or the poses change, and the subjects are ready, then takes the picture. But one thing not everyone likes is that each time the photo is captured, the camera flash blinks. This is meant to be a visual clue that lets you know the shot has been taken. However, you can control how the flash behaves during these automatic capture sessions by configuring a setting. To do so, you’ll go to Settings > Camera > Flash During Capture and toggle the switch off if you prefer.

articles.headline: What does an NPU do and why do so many laptops have them?
keyFacts: Most new mid-range and premium laptops now include a neural processing unit to run artificial intelligence workloads efficiently using minimal power.
Laptop manufacturers added these chips primarily to meet Microsoft certification requirements for Windows AI features, according to the article.
Few applications currently utilize the hardware, leaving the processing capacity largely unused on most consumer devices.
body: What does an NPU do and why do so many laptops have them?
Almost nothing uses it yet.

Bought a new laptop recently? Chances are that it's equipped with an NPU, a chip you're almost certainly not using. The NPU, or Neural Processing Unit, is a block of silicon that runs AI workloads at a fraction of the power a CPU or GPU needs. Roughly 2W compared to well over 100W that standard laptop discrete graphics need to do the same job. While they're not yet found in all laptops, they're now pretty much standard in mid-range and premium machines.

Advisory firm Gartner reckons that AI-capable PCs, like these NPU-equipped laptops, make up more than half of total global shipments. The reason we're seeing this isn't because buyers want or need them, but to align with certification requirements. Back in 2024, Microsoft pretty much dictated that laptop makers will need to hit 40 TOPS (the measure of how quickly an NPU can chew through AI math) of dedicated NPU performance with new machines, or risk losing access to new Windows AI features. NPU hardware is now flying off the shelves as a result, but software is lagging behind.
NPUs are used for AI inference

An NPU's job is to accelerate inference. That's the "run this model" phase rather than the GPU-powered "train this model" phase. Neural networks rely heavily on two kinds of computation to do this: matrix multiplication and nonlinear activation functions. NPUs are purpose-built to execute those operations as quickly and efficiently as possible, but that comes at the cost of some general-purpose CPU and GPU flexibility.

Let's consider the example of using background blur on a video call. Most of us have used this, and it can run on either a CPU or GPU. But both draw a lot of power, generating heat and sapping battery life on a thin portable. An NPU performs the same work using a fraction of the energy, so features like webcam effects can run continuously without draining the battery or spinning up fans.

NPUs are obviously no good for training AI models, and to run large local LLMs like Llama 70B, you'll still need a discrete GPU with a decent chunk of video memory. They're also not needed for services like ChatGPT or Gemini because those run on provider infrastructure. Their actual use case, at least for now, is a small number of always-on and low-power use cases like webcam effects, noise suppression, real-time translation and local search indexing.
How to tell if your laptop has an NPU

The reason we're seeing so many laptops featuring NPUs is because of Microsoft's Copilot + PC certification. Laptop makers can only earn it and unlock certain on-device Windows AI features if their laptops have a 40 TOPS NPU, plus 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. That 40 TOPS figure also has to come from the NPU, not a GPU; a mid-range laptop RTX 4050 offers north of 190 TOPS from its tensor cores. That doesn't count.

Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite and Plus chips were the first to market with a 45 TOPS Hexagon NPU. That was soon followed by Intel's Lunar Lake with up to 48 TOPS, and AMD's Ryzen AI 300 at 50 TOPS. Intel's newer Panther Lake processors, known as Core Ultra Series 3, come with a 50 NPU TOPS on Intel's 18A process. Later this year, Qualcomm has since pushed that to as much as 85 TOPS with Snapdragon X2 Elite, more than double Microsoft's specified minimum. Every generation has ratcheted the number higher even though software to consume those TOPS remains scarce. Soon, AI laptops may well be the only option available, making NPUs unavoidable. We've already seen Dell stuff an enterprise-grade NPU into its Pro Max Plus laptop.

If you've got an NPU-equipped laptop, you can see its utilization rate via Task Manager on Windows 11. On my laptop — a 2024 ASUS Zenbook Duo UX8406 in a 32GB RAM configuration — this sits at zero, and I'd imagine that to be the case on all casual user machines.

Alas, the list of apps that lean on the NPU remains short: Windows Studio Effects, Live Captions, Recall and Click to Do, Teams and Zoom noise suppression and a handful of Adobe Creative Cloud features.
An NPU in action

To see how much of my 34 TOPS Intel AI Boost NPU a local model would hog, I downloaded Mistral 7B, a fairly decent, efficient open-source model and ran it via Intel's OpenVINO toolkit. I then asked it to generate 2,500 words on neural processing units.

Although my machine has 34 platform TOPS combined across the CPU, GPU and NPU, only 11 are dedicated to the NPU. Mistral 7B pegged the NPU at 98 percent while the CPU sat at three percent. Text generation worked, and while 11 TOPS doesn't leave much headroom for a model of that size, my laptop remained fast and responsive.

You can see how this compares to running the same local model off the NPU using Ollama. CPU utilization jumped to 52 percent with memory use holding at around 17GB of my 32GB capacity. If I were running other CPU-intensive workloads, my laptop would've ground to a halt. That's the point of an NPU: It handles an AI workload without impacting the rest of the system. But it required a specific toolkit and technical knowledge to get there in this instance; very little software natively supports it.

articles.headline: From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

The new release will feature updated graphics, new levels, music, cutscenes, and secrets.
The publisher stated that there is currently no release date attached to the upcoming remaster.
body: Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff."

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

articles.headline: Duffy criticizes FAA telecommunications provider L3Harris for mishap that led to ground stop
keyFacts: A nationwide flight ground stop occurred Friday after an L3Harris contractor switching telecommunications lines overloaded FAA systems, officials said.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy criticized L3Harris and stated he needs more funding to switch to other telecommunications providers.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said full flight operations are expected to recover by Sunday after thousands of Saturday cancellations.
body: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy pointed his frustration at the nationwide ground stop Friday night at telecommunications provider L3Harris, claiming he is “stuck” with the company until funding requests are approved for other companies to step in for upgrades.

Duffy held a press conference on Saturday at the Department of Transportation and said the halt in flights was due to a mishap during which an L3Harris contractor was switching telecommunications lines from copper wire to fiber optic cable.

“The work happening was due to the age of the copper wire that we were replacing. It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down, so we had to switch it over from old copper,” Duffy said.
When the contractor installed the new router, the new technology appeared to overload the air traffic control system, leading officials to call for the grounding of all flights.

“We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was give us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar feeds,” Duffy said.
Federal Aviation Administration administrator Bryan Bedford later said the fiber installation error did not cause a blackout in the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure .

“What we had were random reports from different facilities of certain frequencies that were going in and out, and requiring them to switch between primaries and backup switching,” Bedford said. “Now, if that had been a single facility, we would have just worked through it. But when we saw it go to two, three, 10, 17 facilities, that’s when we started to realize there was something much larger going on here. And since we couldn’t explain it quickly, that’s when we went to the national ground stop.”
Now, Duffy said investigators are working to determine if the fault is on the L3Harris contractor or the equipment itself.

“What we’re working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installation error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router?” Duffy said. “We haven’t determined what the fault was.”

L3Harris is the major technology integrator and managed-service provider for the FAA and has been the sole provider for over 20 years. Duffy later said additional funding would allow the FAA to move on from L3Harris, but for now that is not the case.

“With our new architecture, with the money that we’re requesting, we will work with the greatest telecom companies in the world, which will be AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen,” he said. “They’re all working with us on the new architecture. But in the meantime, until I can build that, I’m stuck with L3 Harris, who owns this network.”
Duffy said “we don’t believe” the error was the result of a cyberattack. Bedford also said there is no indication that artificial intelligence was involved in the incident.

“This was an FAA system that didn’t meet the moment,” he said. “Our contractor didn’t meet the moment, or the equipment didn’t meet the moment, and caused the outages. I’ve been talking about this for almost two years, and I’ve been asking Congress for money.”

Congress already approved $12.5 billion for air traffic control modernization through Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, but Duffy has since said the initial investment was not enough. President Donald Trump previously requested $30 billion in funding for the modernization effort, though Duffy upped his ask Friday to $50 billion to complete the overhaul.

While there is more work to be done and additional money to be funded, Duffy emphasized that the DOT is already utilizing its current finances to bring telecommunications systems up to date. He explained that 69% of copper communication wires have been updated with fiber, among several other modernization efforts.

“We can’t continue on technology of the [1980s],” Duffy said. “I mean, we spend over $200 million a year in obsolescence fees. We have to pay to use these old copper wires. We have to get off of them. They’re less reliable. So we have to make the transition, and we’re making the transition not because we want to spend money. We’re making the transition because it’s safer and it’s more resilient.”
FAA’S MODERNIZATION PUSH FACES RENEWED SCRUTINY AFTER NATIONWIDE OUTAGE: WHAT TO KNOW
As for flight operations for the rest of the weekend, Bedford said flights should resume to normal by Sunday, but thousands of flights will be canceled on Saturday.

“We do anticipate somewhere between four and 5,000 of the 41,000 flights that are scheduled today likely will cancel, so we will still have delays and cancellations today,” Bedford said. “But that will set us up for a full recovery tomorrow. And based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday.”

articles.headline: Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop
keyFacts: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that a nationwide FAA ground stop resulted from routine maintenance replacing outdated copper wire with a fiber optic line.
A newly installed router flooded air traffic control systems with over 1,000 connection attempts every few seconds, disrupting radar feeds and plane communications.
Secretary Duffy called on Congress for additional funding to modernize the Air Traffic Control system following the incident.
body: At a press conference today, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that Friday’s nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA was related to work replacing outdated copper wire with a fiber optic line at a “remote FAA facility.” The secretary said that this was “routine maintenance,” rather than the result of a major modernization effort. He told reporters that it was “such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down,” necessitating the upgrade.
Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop
Issues with a new router related to a fiber optic upgrade grounded thousands of flights on Friday.

What wasn’t clear, according to Secretary Duffy, was the root cause of the problem. He said that it could have been faulty hardware, a misconfigured router, or “incompetence” on the part of contractor L3Harris. Regardless, what followed was the newly installed router “flooding” other routers in the Air Traffic Control system. Duffy said that there were “over 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,” causing disruption to radar feeds and communication with planes.

Secretary Duffy also took the opportunity to call on additional funding from Congress for modernizing the Air Traffic Control system, and to tout the work the FAA has done so far. “We are building, we are building safely, but we are building fast,” he said, but said that Congress had only given him a “partial payment” to complete the necessary work.

articles.headline: Poindexter faces sexual harassment investigation after defeating Max Miller
keyFacts: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced an independent investigation into a sexual harassment allegation against recently elected Representative-elect Brian Poindexter.
Two political action committees withdrew their endorsements of Poindexter after receiving a report of alleged harassment involving a campaign volunteer.
Poindexter is scheduled to be sworn into office on January 3 and has not stated that he will step aside.
body: House Democrats’ campaign arm is investigating a sexual harassment allegation against Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter , the Ohio Democrat who unseated Republican Rep. Max Miller less than two weeks ago in one of the cycle’s most closely watched House races.

The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee said Friday it had hired an independent firm to examine the allegation. DCCC Executive Director Julie Merz said in a statement that the committee had been made aware of the allegations and takes them seriously.

The complaint first surfaced in the final days before the Nov. 3 election, when Blue Dog PAC and the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC received a report of alleged harassment involving Poindexter. The two groups, which had endorsed him from opposite wings of the party, said they informed the DCCC and connected the accuser with legal advocacy and support services.

Both PACs have since pulled their endorsements of Poindexter pending the outcome of the investigation. In a joint statement, the groups said the accuser had asked that no details be disclosed publicly and wanted to decide for herself how to proceed while protecting herself.
The woman’s identity has not been made public, and she has not commented publicly. The nature of the alleged conduct has not been disclosed.

Poindexter’s campaign described the cited statement to CNN as “an innocuous compliment to a volunteer.” A campaign spokesperson said Poindexter later learned the remark had made the volunteer uncomfortable and that the campaign felt terrible about it, adding that neither Poindexter nor the campaign wants anyone to feel uncomfortable. The campaign said it had also worked with an outside human resources firm on the matter.

Poindexter had quietly been removed from the endorsement lists of two Democratic groups on Thursday, an unusual turn for a newly elected lawmaker who had drawn support from both the party’s progressive and centrist caucuses. The reason for the removals was not public at the time.

Poindexter, a union ironworker and former Brook Park city councilman, flipped Ohio’s 7th Congressional District, which covers Cleveland’s southern suburbs, giving Democrats a pickup in territory that has traditionally leaned Republican. The Associated Press called the race for Poindexter on election night.

The DCCC added Poindexter to its “Red to Blue” program in August, touting his working-class and labor credentials as it poured resources into the race. He campaigned on affordability, healthcare, and labor issues and outraised Miller, bringing in about $3.72 million to Miller’s $3.32 million as of Nov. 2.

Miller, a two-term Republican and former Trump White House aide, entered the general election weakened by domestic abuse allegations from his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, the daughter of Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH). Miller has denied the allegations, and the House Ethics Committee opened an investigation into his conduct.

The controversy prompted Ohio’s two Republican senators, Moreno and Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH), to call on Miller to step aside. Miller stayed in the race, retaining the support of President Donald Trump .
PUSH FOR NEW DEMOCRATIC LEADERSHIP OVERSHADOWS CELEBRATIONS AT DENVER CONFAB

Poindexter is scheduled to be sworn in Jan. 3 along with the rest of the incoming House freshman class, and has not indicated that he will step aside over the allegation. If a member-elect resigns before taking office, the state’s governor must call a special election to fill the seat.
The Washington Examiner has reached out to Poindexter’s campaign, the DCCC, Blue Dog PAC, the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC, and Miller for comment.

body: There are plenty of things to sell in ROB RUN , and managing your cargo efficiently will make you richer in quick time. These items are harder to manage since you can’t fit them in your backpack.

Unlike specific loot, Cargo is an umbrella term used for any item that you can’t fit inside the bag. Hence, the only option is to carry it in your arms. This creates an issue since you can’t equip any weapons when you’re carrying Cargo.

However, there’s a possible way to mitigate this problem with the use of vehicles. If you have free space in your vehicle, you can then shift the Cargo to that spot. This will now free up your hands without having to leave the valuable loot behind.

articles.headline: COP31: Protesters, UN urge swift climate deal
keyFacts: The UN climate chief urged delegates at the COP31 summit in Turkey to avoid tactical delays and reach a climate deal.
Thousands of activists protested in Antalya to demand climate action and express frustration over delayed government commitments.
A first draft of a deal text is expected to emerge next week, according to Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen.
body: The United Nations' top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey to "avoid tactical delays" that would prevent a deal to stop global warming.
Delegates from more than 200 nations are gathered in the Mediterranean city of Antalya with the core goal of preventing the planet from warming by 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit).
Downtown, thousands of civil society and environmental activists from around the world protested against the consequences of climate change.
What did the UN climate chief say?
Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), said getting an agreement is "tough but vital work."
"There is no collective success without compromise from every party," he added.
"As we head into the second week, I urge parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and to avoid tactical delays."
Climate protest draws activists from around the world
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of protesters marched through Antalya on Saturday for climate protection and human rights, according to organizers.
Many were dismayed at the lack of progress and how the climate crisis is taking a back seat.

"The pursuit of profit at all costs continues to set the [global] agenda [and] govern the trajectory of our world, so there is a need to push back," environmental activist Zaki Mamdoo from South Africa told DW.
Luisa Nebauer, the main organizer of Germany's Fridays for Future movement, lamented that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was absent from the conference, along with several other European leaders.
"We won't have a chance to solve any of the crises as long as our planet is destabilizing by the hour," Nebauer told DW. "We must show up!"
Turkish authorities permitted the rally to go ahead, in a country that often bans large public gatherings.
Alongside the march, a parallel "People's Climate Summit" involving hundreds of domestic and international civil society groups takes place in Antalya this weekend.
Climate crisis pushed down agenda

With inflation, wars, deindustrialization and debt being seen as bigger immediate threats, many governments are watering down their commitments to the clean energy transition, along with the billions required to help developing nations to adapt.
The United States has snubbed the talks for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called climate change a hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.
Delegates also face pressure from large fossil-fuel-producing nations to avoid setting stricter targets for a faster phaseout of oil and gas.
Climate advocates in Antalya are growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of commitment and delaying tactics preventing an ambitious deal.
COP31 is seeking to unlock finance and investment, reduce the use of so-called super-pollutants and methane and ensure food security.
Turkey seeks electrification deal
Host Turkey is, meanwhile, pushing a plan to expand global electrification. Yet, some environmental groups are disappointed the proposal doesn't push increased electricity use from renewable sources.
A UN report last month warned that, within a few years, the world is set to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming.
The figure, set at COP21 in 2015, is the threshold beyond which most scientists believe the world will see increasingly extreme effects of climate change.
A first draft of a deal text is expected to emerge next week, according to Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen.

articles.headline: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
keyFacts: A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.
The maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, Duffy said.
Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure.
body: - Published
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.
Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment.
The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.
Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days.
Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said.
The US has "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he added.
"It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said.

The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons.
Bryan Bedford, who heads the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), told the same news conference: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI related."
No flights were allowed to take off from the continental US for more than four hours from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday.
More than 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed in the US on Saturday, according to tracking website Flight Aware, as knock-on disruption continues.

In some cases, passengers were left stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to the gates. Some international flights were allowed to depart US airports, in an apparent effort to clear space.
Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure.
US President Donald Trump has requested $30.1bn for the upgrades. Both chambers of Congress are currently controlled by the Republican Party.

Former TSA Administrator John Pistole told the BBC that "the fact that they were able to get it restarted in four-and-a-half hours is good news - it shows a resilience in the system - but what's to say it's not going to happen tomorrow?"
A nationwide ground stop has only been ordered one other time since all flights were banned from take-off for several days following the 11 September 2001 attacks.

articles.headline: White House lawyer's hardball warning to Dems has legal experts on both sides questioning one key threat
keyFacts: White House counsel William Scharf warned Democratic Representative Robert Garcia in a letter that congressional investigations could cross into criminal misconduct if used to harass administration officials.
Legal experts questioned the White House's threat of criminal indictments, noting that criminal prosecutions face a high bar and oversight activities enjoy constitutional protections.
Legal experts stated that the administration is within its rights to challenge individual subpoenas through appropriate legal processes.
body: Counsel to the president William Scharf sent a letter to House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform ranking member California Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia Nov. 9, warning Democrats against running afoul of their allotted powers pertaining to investigations and subpoenas .

The letter put Democratic lawmakers on notice to remind them of the "foundational limits that the Constitution imposes on congressional investigations and subpoenas" and suggesting that their actions could cross the line of criminal misconduct. Garcia, who is poised to chair the committee next year when Democrats gain the House majority, responded to the letter suggesting that the president has "something to hide."

Legal experts from across the political spectrum who spoke to Fox News Digital suggested that, while the White House is within its rights to challenge individual subpoenas, it faces significant obstacles if it decides to seek criminal indictments related to Garcia's oversight activities.

"In short, the administration can assert privileges, negotiate over requests and challenge particular subpoenas through the appropriate legal process, but criminal prosecutions are, to mix metaphors, a very different animal that face a higher bar," Ilya Shapiro, director of constitutional studies at the right-of-center Manhattan Institute, told Fox News Digital.
AG BLANCHE CLASHES WITH ANCHOR ASKING WHETHER IT'S HIS 'JOB' TO DEFEND THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

Congressional investigations also enjoy protections under the Constitution's Speech or Debate Clause, which the Supreme Court has held shields lawmakers from judicial interference when their investigative activities fall within the legitimate legislative sphere.

Shapiro explained that Democrats who are "promising indiscriminate subpoenas are inviting challenges to their demands" as congressional committees "must act within their jurisdiction, respect witnesses’ constitutional rights and connect investigations to a legitimate legislative purpose."
Garcia, however, maintains that his calls for investigation are totally consistent with his constitutional authority as a lawmaker.

"Let’s be clear: Congress' authority comes from Article I of the Constitution, not from the permission of the White House . Congress has wide latitude to conduct investigations and oversight, an authority inherent in the power to legislate," Garcia said in his statement .

"The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse. The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers," Garcia stated.

Scharf sent the letter a week after Democrats issued statements and social media posts on calling for subpoenas and impeachment trials for Trump administration officials after Republicans suffered a major loss during the 2026 midterms . At the time, some pointed out that Republicans used similar language to call for investigations into Democratic officials.

Hans von Spakovsky, a senior legal fellow at Advancing American Freedom and a constitutional law expert, told Fox News Digital that Scharf is correct in his assertion that Garcia's investigations cannot be motivated by simple spite, but suggested that the White House may run into problems if they try to get criminal charges to stick.

"Scharf is correct in his citation of Watkins v. U.S. that the Supreme Court has held that congressional investigations not connected to a legitimate legislative purpose and whose only intent is harassment and trying to seize personal, private information are unconstitutional and beyond the power of Congress," von Spakovsky wrote in an email. "Problem is that I am not sure what criminal statutes, if any, could be applied. There are statutes over harassment of federal officials, 18 U.S.C. 111, 115, but those require physical threats. What the Watkins precedent holds is that the courts cannot enforce subpoenas issued by Congress that are part of an improper, unconstitutional investigation."
TOP DEM ON COMMITTEE FIRES BACK AFTER WHITE HOUSE COUNSEL WARNS AGAINST OVERREACH AMID INVESTIGATION THREATS

"No statute makes oversight a crime, and Scharf’s letter doesn't say one does. Its point is that a committee's process doesn't shield conduct that would be a crime for anyone else. Conspiring to intimidate federal officers out of doing their jobs falls under 18 U.S.C. 372," Will Chamberlain, senior counsel at the right-of-center Article III Project, told Fox News Digital. "Congress's oversight authority is broad but not unlimited. There is no congressional power to expose for the sake of exposure and any investigation requires a valid legislative purpose. Congressional investigative activity conducted in an official capacity wouldn't be prosecutable."
He added that, what could be prosecutable, would be a separate conspiracy to intimidate federal officials "evidenced by threats, press releases, things of that nature."
Molly Nixon, a senior fellow at the libertarian Cato Institute, had broadly similar thoughts.

"White House Counsel is correct that courts have required congressional investigations to serve a legitimate legislative purpose, though the constitutional boundaries of that requirement are not as clear as Scharf asserts. I don’t think the letter is on solid ground when it makes the leap to suggesting potential criminality," she told Fox News Digital.
DEMS PIVOT FROM ‘AFFORDABILITY’ PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

"We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government. Recent public statements underscore these concerns. You and your congressional colleagues have asserted that they will issue subpoenas to harass, threaten, and deter dedicated members of the Administration from further service," wrote Scharf.

"Compulsory process is a power Congress has for oversight functions, and only for oversight functions. Abusive threats and public statements about the indiscriminate issuance of subpoenas, along with threats directed at prospective targets within the Administration make it abundantly clear that any forthcoming investigative processes will be deployed to harass and aggrandize, rather than to advance any legitimate legislative end," the letter continued.

"Beyond being inconsistent with the clear, well-recognized constitutional limitations on your investigative functions, threats to executive branch officials designed to deter them from public service, or process designed merely to abuse or instill fear in the recipient may cross the line into blatant criminality," the letter continued. "And issuing unlawful subpoenas with the intention of depriving citizens of their constitutional rights and privileges may warrant further investigation."

Those further investigations, however, are unlikely to result in criminal charges, according Devon Ombres, senior director for courts and legal policy at the left-of-center Center for American Progress.

"You know, I don't think that there is any reasonable basis for the administration to argue that Congress cannot undertake its constitutional obligations of conducting oversight, and I can't imagine that there's any type of criminal statute that would apply in this context," he said in a phone call. "That's not to say that this DOJ won't try and shoehorn something in, as they've already done, but I don't think that Scharf has a legal leg to stand on."
While criminal charges would face significant legal obstacles, Ombres says he fully expects the Trump administration to try blocking the subpoenas through lawsuits.
"The White House and the DOJ is going to throw everything, including the kitchen sink, at subpoenas," said Ombres.

articles.headline: Do you like mob tagging in oldschool MMOs, or are you done with fighting for quest credit?
keyFacts: PC Gamer columnist Harvey stated that mob tagging in massively multiplayer online games is divisive among players.
The author argued that mob tagging drives social interaction by encouraging players to form groups and converse.
The author acknowledged that mob tagging is frustrating during game launches when player populations are heavily concentrated.
body: This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

I've been having a pleasant time with WoW: Forever (and by that, I mean it has consumed nearly every waking moment of my life). One thing, however, has been made pretty clear: Mob tagging, that is, only giving kill credit to the first player (or group) to damage a mob, is divisive.

One side of the fence—my side, I'm afraid—does see mob tagging as a necessary evil in an MMO that's trying to drive social interaction. Videogames, particularly ones that are incentivising you to group up, are kind of meant to be a pain in the butt sometimes; if you've got a "kill 20" quest and there another person there, the fact you might get in each other's way if you don't group up, and have a jollier time if you do, is a net good.

I have more complicated thoughts on item drop quests being bad in a group, sure. And I'd like it if Blizzard's layering technology was a little more merciful. But, overall, I'm all for it. Nearly every single person I've thrown an invite to has grouped up with me, and I've even (gasp) had conversations with strangers. Pleasant ones!

Some of them are even on my friends list now, and it is, I think, a point in my favour that I would have largely ignored every single person I am now regularly chatting to if mob tagging wasn't a thing.

However, I do get the other side of the fence, in that it is absolutely a pain in the ass. Particularly in a game that's just launched, where the playerbase is nowhere near as spread out as it needs to be. There's a thin difference between good social banter being encouraged and "for the love of god, I just need one troll fetish, why are these mystics spread 30 feet apart, thank god I farmed my mount before I did this".

A difference, it's important to state, that is more often broken in a game that's so wildly popular as Forever is right now. Mob tagging holds up when it's you and a handful of other players in a questing environment: It's less defensible when there's 30 of you and it's a "loot X" quest so grouping wouldn't help, anyway.
So I ask you, fine readers of Terminally Online: Do you think tagging mobs is fine in an oldschool MMO, or is it an archaic thing of the past to be done away with?
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
If you've got deeper thoughts on this, let me know in the comments below!

Harvey's history with games started when he first begged his parents for a World of Warcraft subscription aged 12, though he's since been cursed with Final Fantasy 14-brain and a huge crush on G'raha Tia. He made his start as a freelancer, writing for websites like Techradar, The Escapist, Dicebreaker, The Gamer, Into the Spine—and of course, PC Gamer. He'll sink his teeth into anything that looks interesting, though he has a soft spot for RPGs, soulslikes, roguelikes, deckbuilders, MMOs, and weird indie titles. He also plays a shelf load of TTRPGs in his offline time. Don't ask him what his favourite system is, he has too many.

articles.headline: Democrat wins Alaska governor’s seat for first time in nearly 30 years
keyFacts: Former state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won Alaska's governor race, becoming the state's first Democratic governor elected since 1998.
This victory expanded Democratic control to 30 US governorships alongside major congressional gains that shifted power away from Republicans.
Kreiss-Tomkins pledged to assemble a governing cabinet composed of Democrats, Republicans, and independents.
body: Democrats have captured Alaska’s governor’s seat for the first time in nearly three decades, marking another major victory for their party in a midterm election period that has dramatically shifted political power across the US.

Former Alaska state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republican opponents, including a candidate backed by Donald Trump, becoming the first Democrat elected governor of Alaska since 1998.

His victory – called by the Associated Press on Friday, 10 days after the polls closed – adds to a growing list of Democratic gains nationwide, bringing the party’s total to 30 US governorships. Democrats have also taken control of governor’s offices in several other longtime Republican strongholds, including Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.
Kreiss-Tomkins, widely known as JKT, secured the win having mounted a political comeback three years after departing the Alaska house of representatives.
The 37-year-old traveled extensively throughout the state during his campaign, building support around economic concerns and a promise to change the direction of Alaska’s government.

His platform centered on tackling affordability, ensuring full funding for public education, and requiring all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income taxes. He also pushed for a temporary halt to new datacenter developments until state lawmakers establish regulations governing their construction.
Throughout the campaign, Kreiss-Tomkins sharply criticized the leadership of outgoing the Republican governor, Mike Dunleavy, arguing that Alaska had become “broken” during his eight years in office.
“Alaskans are hungry for change,” Kreiss-Tomkins said. “We’ve been running the same campaign since we launched in February, and I don’t take anyone’s vote for granted.”

Among his criticisms was the deterioration of the state’s ferry system, which Kreiss-Tomkins said had been left in disarray as service to numerous communities was drastically reduced. The ferry network serves as a critical transportation link for communities in south-east Alaska that lack road connections, including some with limited access to air travel.

Despite his criticism of the outgoing administration, Kreiss-Tomkins presented himself as a leader willing to work across political divisions. He pledged to assemble a cabinet that includes Democrats, Republicans and independents.

Unlike most states, Alaska allows voters to rank candidates by preference through ranked-choice voting – a system that also permits multiple candidates from the same political party to run against one another.
But Kreiss-Tomkins avoided the need for additional rounds of vote counting after winning more than 50% of first-choice votes, securing an outright victory.

The Alaska result comes just days after Democrats scored another major gubernatorial win in staunchly conservative Kansas, where the Democratic state senator Cindy Holscher narrowly defeated the Republican state senate president, Ty Masterson.

Masterson, who received Trump’s endorsement, faced a campaign in which Holscher repeatedly highlighted his ties to the Republican president. At the same time, Holscher maintained that she would remain willing to cooperate with the Trump administration on issues where common ground could be found.
The back-to-back victories in Alaska and Kansas underscore the scale of Democratic gains in what has become a nationwide electoral shift.

The party’s long-anticipated “blue wave” has now materialized, with Democrats flipping eight seats in the US Senate, gaining more than two dozen seats in the House and significantly expanding their control of governors’ offices after the 3 November midterms.

Such gains have handed Democrats a strong majority in Congress for the latter half of Trump’s second presidency, delivering a major shift in the balance of power in Washington and state governments across the US.

Meanwhile, with few ballots left to count for Alaska’s midterm US Senate election, Democrat Mary Peltola on Saturday was leading Republican incumbent Dan S Sullivan, Alaska Public Media reported. That had prompted MS Now to characterize that Senate race as “leans Democratic”.

Beside Alaska and Kansas, the Democratic party won gubernatorial elections over Republicans in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas, putting them in control of a majority of governorships for the first time since 2010. Gina Hinojosa is the first Democrat to be elected governor of Texas in 35 years – and also the state’s first Hispanic governor.

A major factor in the GOP’s midterm defeat is the unpopularity of Trump, whom most Republican lawmakers clung to even as polls indicated voters did not support his immigration crackdown, tariffs, the war with Iran or his signature domestic policy bill.

articles.headline: Magnificent Wales beat New Zealand for first time since 1953
keyFacts: Wales defeated New Zealand 35-28 in a Nations Championship match to secure their first victory against the All Blacks since 1953.
Steve Tandy's team built a 35-21 lead through nine total tries before holding off New Zealand with a resilient defensive display in the final quarter.
The historic win ended a 34-match losing sequence against New Zealand that stretched back 73 years.
body: - Published
Nations Championship
Wales (21) 35
Tries: T Williams, Lake, Griffin, James, Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow 5
New Zealand (21) 28
Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4.
Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953.

In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins.
The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes.

Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time.
Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back.
The remarkable Wales defence followed as they held up the All Blacks three times over the line to stop New Zealand scoring, to evoke wild celebrations.
Good things come to those who wait
Wales had won the first three games in this fixture in 1905, 1935 and 1953 but have had to wait more than seven decades for the next.
In 1953 the New Zealand dollar did not exist, Cardiff was not the capital city of Wales and tries were only worth three points.
Sections of the New Zealand media had belittled Welsh rugby before the game, while some bookmakers offered odds of 20-1 for a Wales victory.
Legends such as Sir Gareth Edwards, Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams, JPR Williams, Barry John and Phil Bennett had never enjoyed success against New Zealand in a Welsh jersey.
Now Tandy's class of 2026 have written their own chapter in Welsh rugby's history.
The 55,152 was the lowest crowd in the 14 matches between Wales and New Zealand at the Principality Stadium. The fans who stayed away will regret it because it was a day to say "I was there".
Welsh rugby has been in the doldrums for so long, on and off the field, but will hope this famous victory can help galvanise the nation.
This was one of the finest performances in Welsh rugby history and a world apart from the display in the 28-21 win against Japan last weekend.

New Zealand might regret failing to take advantage of France's victory against South Africa on Friday night but they still leapfrog the Springboks to top the southern section with one weekend of regular matches remaining.
Fast start for Wales as hosts dare to dream
Wales made four changes to the side that beat Japan, with Taine Basham making his first Test start in four years by replacing injured number eight Aaron Wainwright.
Leicester wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb was preferred to Josh Adams, who scored two tries against Japan, while lock Adam Beard and flanker Botham came in for Ben Carter and Alex Mann.
New Zealand made eight starting swaps from the team that beat Scotland 43-21, with full-back Beauden Barrett handed the Test captaincy for the first time in his 149th international.
New Zealand's haka was the usual piece of theatre as the All Blacks were lit up by a spotlight and Wales in red.
The hosts reacted quickest from the start with prop Nicky Smith winning a turnover before an excellent long pass from Williams released Rees-Zammit.
The wing chipped ahead and Williams, who New Zealand coach Dave Rennie had highlighted as a pre-match dangerman, pounced for the try.
Wales followed this up with a well-worked forward move and captain Lake latched onto a flat Williams pass to crash over.
It was the first time Wales had led New Zealand by 14 points and the home crowd began to dream.
New Zealand bounce back to level the scores
New Zealand seemed shell-shocked but regathered themselves, and Ratima strolled over for an easy try from an attacking line-out.
Rennie stated before the match they needed to eliminate the threat of Morgan at the breakdown, but they failed to do that when the Wales flanker forced a turnover penalty.
This provided the platform for New Zealand-born Wales full-back Blair Murray to release Rees-Zammit, with only good defensive work by Beauden Barrett preventing a try.
New Zealand's defence kept Wales at bay with some important turnovers before a breathless period of play followed with both sides throwing wild passes.

Once matters had settled down, New Zealand made an unusual decision to go for a scrum in the Wales 22 after being given a penalty. This backfired when the visitors were penalised and it provided the hosts with fresh momentum.
The Wales line-out, which broke down against Japan with six throws going astray, was excellent in the opening quarter and provided the foundation for the third try.
After centre Max Llewellyn was initially denied under the All Blacks' posts, prop Griffin popped up for his second try in two weeks.
New Zealand learned from their earlier error by going for an attacking line-out rather than a scrum and Sititi, who was player of the match in this fixture 12 months ago, eventually dived over.
The All Blacks demonstrated their doggedness at the breakdown by forcing two penalties, while the home line-out began to creak with two overthrows.
New Zealand began to grind away and wing Fineanganofo flopped over with Mo'unga's conversion levelling the scores at half-time.
Wales buck history trend to celebrate victory
This was the time we assumed the script would follow the familiar tale of New Zealand pulling away. Wales had other ideas.
The hosts began the second half in the same fashion as the first, with scrum-half Williams again the architect as his long pass allowed James to crash over.
Morgan again tormented New Zealand to force another turnover penalty. Wales decided to go for the try and the decision was justified.
Williams' long pass allowed Rees-Zammit to cross for the fifth try which is the highest amount scored by Wales against New Zealand.
Two tries inside the first six minutes in the first half for Wales. A pair of scores inside eight minutes in the second.
New Zealand again regrouped, with flanker Lakai burrowing over as the All Blacks came within seven points.

Lakai almost inspired a fifth Kiwi try with a fine break but replacement prop Gareth Thomas had other ideas by expertly holding up Sititi over the Wales line, before Botham repeated the feat on hooker Asafo Aumua.

Replacement Wales eight Taine Plumtree gained two important turnovers before Tandy decided to take off his half-backs Williams and Costelow, with Ospreys duo Dan Edwards and Reuben Morgan-Williams tasked to see out the final 16 minutes.
Edwards and Morgan combined to hold up New Zealand for a third time over the line but the All Blacks onslaught kept coming.
Wales dug deep once more, tapping reserves of strength, discipline and concentration to repel that black wave.
The final whistle delivered the win this side and nation have deserved for so long, reducing players and fans alike to tears of joy.
